gap: The r8 structural finding is genuinely answered and I will not re-litigate it: the hero is now a LEDGER. Four dated rows, four real customer names, untidy amounts, Paid / Overdue / Draft pills, a select-all plus five row checkboxes, a search field with a magnifier, an outlined Filter pill, a USD/EUR/AED toggle, ruled Customer / Date / Amount / Status headers, a total, and a real globe+EN locale control in the navy header so the 'Languages supported 5' chip finally names something that exists. The hero total is even arithmetically correct: 4,820.50 + 12,500.75 + 2,140.25 + 863.40 = 20,324.90, exactly what the panel prints. Drawings do not usually add up, and that detail is worth real credibility. It still loses, on craft inside the frame and on one contradiction the fix created. FIRST, a ghost element sits at the top-left of the table, the single most-read corner of the page: TWO identical rounded search-field rectangles are stacked, an empty tan-outlined one half-tucked under the navy header and, one field-height below it, the real one carrying the magnifier and 'Search invoices'. A screenshot cannot contain a duplicate of its own search box. SECOND, all five checkboxes sit low of their own labels, roughly a third of a row height below the customer name, so each one straddles the ruled separator instead of centring on its row; Wave's checkbox centres cleanly on every one of its six rows. THIRD, the tilt is borrowed from the wrong Wave image. Ours rotates the panel about 7 degrees, and across four columns that staggers one row's cells nearly two full row-heights, so 'Northwind Trading Co.' sits at the same screen height as 'May 09' and '$12,500.75', which are Harbour Point's numbers. The rules do resolve it, but only if the eye consciously tracks the slope. Wave's own answer is the tell: their crisp readable Transactions table is set dead FLAT, and the aggressive 3D tilt is spent only on the home shot that is deliberately blurred and unreadable. We put the decorative tilt on the data image. FOURTH, the r8 chip fault is untouched: 'Currency billing / Any' still tails RIGHT into the sidebar gutter beside 'Total outstanding', while the USD/EUR/AED toggle it should be naming sits in the opposite corner of the panel. FIFTH and worst, the two product mocks now disagree about the product's own books. Hero: Northwind Trading Co. / May 12 / $4,820.50, Harbour Point $12,500.75, Cedar Clinic $2,140.25, Studio Meridian $863.40, total $20,324.90. The 'every market' mock, same four customers, same four dates: $4,820.00, $12,500.00, $2,140.00, $860.00, total $20,320.00. Four rows, four mismatches, under a headline that reads 'Your data stays the same, only the interface changes.' Making the hero untidy without restating the Arabic mock turned the page's two screenshots into two different accounts of what one customer owes, and nothing destroys trust in product imagery faster. SIXTH, mobile is where r8 left it: below the CTA there is only a corner of navy chrome reading 'Invoices EN' plus one chip, no row, no amount, no status, against Wave's two small but complete and legible callouts. A synthetic mock CAN beat a real capture and I am not issuing that as the gap, because our own second mock proves it: flat, horizontal, RTL, browser chrome with three dots and a 'Paper & Pen' title, a real '+ فاتورة جديدة' button, and every cell on a shared baseline. It reads as software. THE FIX: flatten the hero to that second mock's near-zero tilt or cut the rotation to two or three degrees, delete the duplicate search rectangle, centre each checkbox on its row's text baseline, move the 'Currency billing / Any' chip so its tail lands on the USD/EUR/AED toggle, restate the Arabic mock with the SAME four amounts and the same $20,324.90 total so both shots are one product, and lift enough of the panel above the mobile fold to show one complete row with its amount and status pill.
